paper.title: No-regret learning for repeated non-cooperative games with lossy bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated concave N-player game with lossy bandit feedback (regret)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Learning in non-cooperative continuous games: all N players run the algorithm (regret not shown against arbitrary opponents).
unmapped: N-player concave game: each player's utility is concave in its own action and depends on the others' actions
lossy bandit feedback: the utility value is received with probability p_i (i.i.d. Bernoulli), otherwise the action is not updated
learner knows the reception probability p_i (used in the step size)
learner knows a ball B_{r_i}(c_i) inside its action set
settings.definition_quote: Let $p_{i}$ denote the probability that  player $i$  will receive its utility value,  then  the probability of  information loss is $1-p_{i}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated beta-strongly monotone game with lossy bandit feedback (convergence to Nash equilibrium)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Learning in games with an equilibrium (Nash) convergence objective.
unmapped: objective: mean-square convergence of the joint action profile to the Nash equilibrium
lossy bandit feedback with known reception probability p_i
settings.definition_quote: Suppose that  $\mathcal{G}$ is a $\beta-$strongly monotone game on action space $\mathcal{A}$

algorithms.name: OGD-lb (Online Gradient Descent with lossy bandits)
requires_knowledge_of: p_i (feedback reception probability; not needed in the unknown-p variant)
ball B_{r_i}(c_i) inside the action set

symbols.p_i: probability that player i receives its bandit feedback
symbols.w: positive constant in the step size gamma_{i,k} = gamma_k p_i^{-w}
symbols.B_i: Euclidean diameter of player i's action set
symbols.L_i: Lipschitz constant of player i's partial gradient
symbols.G_i: d_i * max |u_i| over the joint action set
symbols.gamma_k: base step size at iteration k (non-increasing)
symbols.gamma_K: base step size at the final iteration

conditions: Assumption 1: compact convex action sets with nonempty interior, utilities concave in own action, partial gradients L_i-Lipschitz
Assumption 2: perturbations and loss indicators independent; indicators i.i.d. over time

source.label: regret
source.quote: Let Assumptions 1-2 hold. Consider the players follow Algorithm 1 with step-size $\gamma_{i,k}=\gamma_{k}p_{i}^{-w}$ and constant $w>0$. Suppose that $\{\gamma_{k}\}$ and $\{\delta_{k}\}$ are non-increasing sequences with $\delta_{1}<\min_{i} r_{i}$. Then for each $i\in \mathcal{N}$, $\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}eg^{(i)}(K)] \leq \frac{p_{i}^{w-1}B_{i}^{2}}{2\gamma_{K}}+\sum_{k=1}^{K}B_{i}L_{i}\sqrt{N}\delta_{k}+\sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{p_{i}^{w-1}}{2\gamma_{k}}\frac{G_{i}^{2}}{\delta_{k}^{2}}\mathbb{E}[\gamma_{i,k}^{2}]

results.notes: Regret is per player in the game, measured against the best fixed own action given the others' realized actions. The paper's K (iterations) is mapped to T. The expectation is outside the max, so this is expected regret.

symbols.p_i: probability that player i receives its bandit feedback
symbols.B_i: Euclidean diameter of player i's action set
symbols.L_i: Lipschitz constant of player i's partial gradient
symbols.G_i: d_i * max |u_i| over the joint action set

source.label: no-regret
source.quote: Consider the players follow Algorithm 1 with $\gamma_{i,k}=1/(k^{b}p_{i})$ and $\delta_{k}={\delta_{1}}k^{-c}$ with $0<b<1$, $0<c<b/2$ and $\delta_{1}<\min_{i} r_{i}$. Then for each $i\in \mathcal{N}$, $\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}eg^{(i)} (K)] \leq \frac{B_{i}^{2}}{2}k^{b}+ \frac{B_{i}L_{i}\sqrt{N}{\delta_{1}}}{1-c}K^{1-c}+\frac{G_{i}^{2}}{2p_{i}^{2}{\delta_{1}^{2}}(1-b+2c)}K^{1-b+2c}+B_{i}L_{i}\sqrt{N}{\delta_{1}}+\frac{G_{i}^{2}}{2p_{i}^{2}{\delta_{1}^{2}}}.

results.notes: The paper prints the first term as k^b. This is evidently a typo for K^b, since the proof gives 1/(2 gamma_K) = K^b/2. The remark notes O(K^{max{b,1-c,1-b+2c}}); with b=3/4 and c=1/4 this gives K^{3/4}.

symbols.beta_mon: strong monotonicity modulus of the game's pseudo-gradient

conditions: quantity is E||hat a_k - a*||^2 at iteration k (mapped to T)

source.label: the2
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions 1, 2, and 4 hold. Consider the players follow Algorithm 1 with $\gamma_{i,k}={1}/({k p_{i}})$ and $\delta_{k}={\delta_{1}}k^{-1/3}$ with $\delta_{1}<\min_{i} r_{i}$. Then $\mathbb{E}[\|\hat{a}_{k}-a^{*}\|^{2}]=\mathcal{O}(k^{-2\min\{\beta, 1/6\}})$.

results.notes: This is a mean-square distance to the Nash equilibrium, not regret. The almost-sure convergence results (Theorems 2 and 4) are qualitative and were not recorded.
